name: What if the plumbing is original and I want to renovate the bathrooms?

mainEntity.name: Can I modernize bathrooms in an older home if the supply and drain lines are still original?
mainEntity.text: Can I modernize bathrooms in an older home if the supply and drain lines are still original?

acceptedAnswer.text: Bathroom renovations are one of the most common places where older-home plumbing problems surface. Original supply lines and drain pipes may still function, but they can also be corroded, restricted, or too small for modern fixtures. That is why plumbing should be inspected before the bathroom design is finalized. If the lines are aging or unreliable, replacing them during the remodel is usually the smarter move because the walls and floors are already open. This prevents a new tile job or vanity install from being disturbed later. Even when full replacement is not necessary, the remodel should verify pressure, venting, shutoff access, and fixture compatibility. The goal is not just a prettier bathroom, but one that works reliably after construction is complete.
acceptedAnswer.description: Yes, but original plumbing should be evaluated before finishing the bathrooms. If pipes are corroded, undersized, or prone to leaks, it is usually better to replace them while the walls and floors are open. Otherwise, new bathroom finishes may need to be removed later for plumbing repairs.
